transcript.text: I received the completed obligor-concentration assessment this morning. The key finding is that the single-obligor limit leaves exactly $4,000,000 of the $6,000,000 invoice pool eligible for financing -- not the full $6,000,000 assumed in the preliminary proposal. Additionally, the approved advance rate for that eligible exposure is exactly 85%, not the 90% advance rate assumed in the preliminary proposal. This assessment has not yet been uploaded to the credit file, so I'm formally disclosing it to the committee now. In practice, this means the facility as preliminarily proposed -- financing 90% of $6,000,000 -- would exceed both our concentration limits and our approved advance rate. The maximum financing under the approved terms would be 85% of $4,000,000, or $3,400,000. I recommend the committee revise the facility terms accordingly before any launch decision is made.

transcript.text: Thank you, Elias. Now I'll share the legal finding I flagged earlier. I received a signed anchor-buyer undertaking in a legal memo this morning. There are two critical requirements that directly contradict the preliminary proposal's assumptions. First, the program must be non-recourse to suppliers -- this directly conflicts with the preliminary proposal's assumption of ordinary supplier recourse. Second, the buyer's payment direction must be acknowledged before the first funding. This memo has not yet been circulated to the committee, so I'm formally disclosing it now. In practice, this means the facility as preliminarily proposed -- with ordinary supplier recourse and no special funding controls -- cannot launch on those terms. The facility terms must be revised to reflect non-recourse to suppliers, and an acknowledgment of the buyer's payment direction must be obtained before any first funding occurs.

transcript.text: Thank you, Nadia. Now I'll share the finance operations perspective. My operations team completed a workflow test this week, and there are two operational constraints that directly impact the preliminary proposal's assumptions about funding and screening controls. First, funding can be released only twice weekly -- not on the continuous basis the preliminary proposal assumes. Second, every invoice requires a 3-business-day hold for duplicate-invoice screening before it can be funded, which means the proposal's assumption of no special screening controls is not operationally feasible. This test result has not yet been recorded in the launch checklist, so I'm formally disclosing it to the committee now. In practice, the facility terms must be revised to reflect that funding is limited to twice-weekly disbursements and that a mandatory 3-business-day duplicate-invoice screening hold applies to every invoice before funding release.
